module.title: Culinary Traditions, Recipes & Kitchen Verbs
module.group: A2.2 - Social Dynamics, Work & Everyday Life
module.objective: Explain cooking recipes, culinary traditions, and preparation steps using kitchen verbs and sequence markers.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Culinary Traditions and Kitchen Verbs
subModules.grammarFocus: Imperatives for recipes and sequence connectors

content.summary: Welcome to the reading mission on culinary traditions and recipes. In this section, you will read short texts about cooking, learn how to understand kitchen instructions, and practice reading strategies like scanning for specific ingredients and sequence words.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Imperative verbs (chop, boil, mix) and sequence words (First, Next, Then, Finally).
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Cooking verbs, ingredients, and measurement words.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Scanning for sequence words and key cooking steps in procedural texts.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of short A2 texts about traditional recipes and cooking steps.
Locate specific details such as ingredients, measurements, and cooking times.
Recognize and practice imperative sentence structures used in recipe instructions.

contextWarmup.prompt: When you follow a recipe to cook something new at home, what is the very first thing you should always do?
options: Read all the ingredients and instructions carefully before starting.
Throw everything into a hot pan immediately without measuring.
Clean your bedroom and wash your clothes.
contextWarmup.explanation: Checking the ingredients and reading instructions first helps you prepare properly and prevents mistakes while cooking.

rules: Use kitchen verbs in the imperative form without a subject to write recipes: 'Chop the onions', 'Boil the water', 'Mix the ingredients'.
Use sequence words to order steps: 'First, wash the vegetables. Next, chop them into small pieces. Then, heat the oil. Finally, serve the dish hot.'
State measurements clearly using measurement words: '2 tablespoons of sugar', '1 cup of flour', '500 grams of chicken', 'a pinch of salt'.

commonTrap.explanation: Learners often start cooking immediately without reading the full ingredient list, which leads to missing items halfway through.
commonTrap.wrong: Starting to fry chicken without checking if you have oil and salt.
commonTrap.correct: Always read the recipe completely and gather all ingredients on the counter before you start cooking.

paragraphs: Cooking traditional food is an important part of family life around the world. In Italy, Sunday lunch is a special event where families gather to enjoy home-cooked meals. Maria loves helping her grandmother in the kitchen every weekend. First, they check the recipe book to make sure they have every ingredient ready on the kitchen table. Maria learns how to chop fresh garlic and slice ripe tomatoes carefully.

Next, they boil water in a large pot for the pasta. While the water is heating, Maria helps mix the flour and eggs for homemade bread. Then, her grandmother shows her how to fry vegetables in a pan and stir the tomato sauce gently. Finally, they bake a sweet dessert in the oven. Cooking together is fun, and sharing delicious food makes family traditions alive and special.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Writing Recipes and Culinary Instructions

content.summary: Practical guide on writing simple recipes, kitchen verbs, and sequence words in English.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Imperative Verbs for Recipes
blueprintItems.example: Chop the onions and slice the tomatoes.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Sequence Words for Steps
blueprintItems.example: First, boil the water. Next, add the pasta.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Measurement Expressions
blueprintItems.example: Add two tablespoons of sugar and one cup of flour.

mechanicsRules.rule: Start recipe instructions with base verbs instead of subjects.
mechanicsRules.why: Recipe steps give direct commands to the cook.

mechanicsRules.rule: Put a comma after sequence words at the beginning of a sentence.
mechanicsRules.badExample: First boil the water in a large pot.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: First, boil the water in a large pot.
mechanicsRules.why: Sequence words like First, Next, and Then need a comma when introducing a step.

mechanicsRules.rule: Capitalize the first letter of every sentence and keep food names lowercase unless they are proper nouns.
mechanicsRules.badExample: then add italian cheese to the pasta.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Then, add Italian cheese to the pasta.
mechanicsRules.why: Italian is a proper adjective, so it needs capitalization.

sampleSentences.en: First, wash the fresh vegetables thoroughly.
sampleSentences.id: Pertama, cuci sayuran segar secara menyeluruh.

sampleSentences.en: Chop the onions into small pieces.
sampleSentences.id: Potong bawang bombay menjadi bagian kecil-kecil.

sampleSentences.en: Add two tablespoons of olive oil to the pan.
sampleSentences.id: Tambahkan dua sendok makan minyak zaitun ke dalam panci.

sampleSentences.en: Finally, serve the delicious soup hot with bread.
sampleSentences.id: Terakhir, sajikan sup yang lezat selagi panas dengan roti.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the affirmative instruction into a negative instruction using 'Don't':
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'Don't' at the beginning of the sentence.
targetAnswers: Don't add salt to the soup.
Do not add salt to the soup.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Negative imperative sentences in English start with 'Don't' or 'Do not' followed by the base verb.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Fix the capitalization and punctuation in this recipe instruction:
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize the first letter and ensure proper punctuation.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Sequence words at the start of a sentence require a comma and capital letter.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct sequence word for the middle cooking step:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Boil the water. _____, add the pasta to the pot.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use a sequence word that means after that.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Words like 'Next' or 'Then' are used for intermediate steps in a recipe.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence using a measurement expression with 'cup':
practicumQuestions.hint: Include 'one cup of' before the ingredient.
targetAnswers: Add one cup of flour to the bowl.
Add a cup of flour to the bowl.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Measurement expressions require a number or article, the unit, 'of', and the ingredient noun.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a complete sentence describing what kitchen action you do with onions:
practicumQuestions.hint: Use an imperative verb and the object noun.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Kitchen actions for vegetables use verbs like 'chop', 'slice', or 'peel'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the error in measurement pluralization in this sentence:
practicumQuestions.hint: Measurement units pluralize when the number is greater than one.
practicumQuestions.explanation: When a number is greater than one (three), the unit (tablespoon) must be pluralized (tablespoons).

practicumQuestions.instruction: Fill in the final sequence word for the last step of the recipe:
practicumQuestions.promptText: _____, serve the hot soup in bowls.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use the sequence word that indicates the final step.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Finally' is the standard sequence word used to introduce the last step in instructions.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change this declarative sentence into an imperative recipe instruction:
practicumQuestions.explanation: Recipe instructions are direct commands, so they omit the subject 'you' and start with the base verb.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a sentence explaining how to heat oil in a pan using the sequence word 'First':
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with 'First,' followed by the imperative action.
targetAnswers: First, heat oil in a pan.
First, heat the oil in the pan.
practicumQuestions.explanation: A correct recipe step combines the sequence word, comma, imperative verb, object, and prepositional phrase.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the punctuation and article in this sentence:
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize the first word, add a comma after the sequence word, and include 'a' before 'pinch'.
targetAnswers: Then, add a pinch of salt.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Expressions like 'pinch of salt' need the article 'a', and sentences must begin with a capital letter and a comma after introductory sequence words.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Culinary Traditions, Recipes & Kitchen Verbs

content.summary: Clear pronunciation and descriptive vocabulary are essential for explaining recipes and sharing culinary traditions at the A2 level.
content.audioGuidance: Focus on clear articulation of kitchen action verbs and natural intonation when giving instructions.

pillars.name: Vowel Clarity
pillars.target: Clear short and long vowels in kitchen verbs
pillars.explanation: Ensure vowels in words like chop, boil, and bake are distinct and easy to understand.

pillars.name: Verb Stress
pillars.explanation: Place natural sentence stress on kitchen verbs to make your directions clear to listeners.

pillars.name: Sentence Flow
pillars.explanation: Connect sequence words like first and then smoothly with the following action verbs.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: The primary stress remains on the first syllable in both forms.
Notice that the main stress stays on the root verb syllable.
Keep the stress strong on the first syllable.
The stress shifts when adding the adjective suffix, landing on the third syllable.
